remediation_records.priority_category: Missing Clinical Prerequisites and Screening Restrictions
remediation_records.current_behavior: Approves Sella CT (CPT 70480) solely on the presence of a sellar, suprasellar, or parasellar mass (`sellar_or_parasellar_mass == True`) without checking if MRI is feasible.
remediation_records.exact_policy_supported_requirement: Sella CT is indicated for evaluation of known sellar and/or parasellar masses WHEN MRI is contraindicated or cannot be performed (Guideline 2056, physical p. 881).
remediation_records.governing_pdf: 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Advanced Imaging v2.pdf
remediation_records.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR SELLA CT

proposed_minimal_correction.summary: Add mandatory MRI contraindication / inability prerequisite condition to existing sellar mass rule.

criteria_spec.description: Known sellar, suprasellar, or parasellar mass requiring bony evaluation or surgical planning
Brain/sella MRI is medically contraindicated or cannot be performed (e.g. non-conditional pacemaker/ICD, ocular metallic foreign body, severe claustrophobia, or scanner weight/dimension limit)

citation_spec.source_quote:
For further evaluation of known sellar and/or parasellar masses
When MRI is contraindicated or cannot be performed

remediation_records.false_approval_risk: High. Approves soft-tissue CT of the sella without preliminary MRI when MRI is the gold standard and safe to perform.
remediation_records.false_denial_risk: Low. If MRI is contraindicated or unavailable and documented, CT is approved.

explicit_policy_requirements: Presence of sellar or parasellar mass
MRI is contraindicated OR cannot be performed
alternative_conditions_or: MRI cannot be performed (claustrophobia, bariatric scanner limit)
cumulative_conditions_and: Sellar mass AND (MRI contraindicated OR cannot be performed)
advisory_or_preferred_language: MRI is the preferred first-line imaging modality for pituitary and sellar soft tissue
exceptions_and_special_populations: Emergency postoperative hemorrhage does not require prior MRI failure
logic_validation.missing_evidence_behavior: UNKNOWN. If MRI contraindication status is unstated, evaluate to INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION.

boundary_value_cases.description: Severe claustrophobia with failed oral sedation documented as inability to perform MRI

regression_assertions: Verify temporal bone CT for hearing loss / mastoiditis (CPT 70480 under other rules) remains unaffected.
Verify brain MRI (CPT 70551-70553) routing remains unaffected.

remediation_records.clinical_service_or_procedure: Upper Extremity CT (Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist, Hand)
remediation_records.current_behavior: Approves Upper Extremity CT (CPT 73200-73202) for persistent joint pain with negative X-ray and conservative therapy without checking MRI contraindication or CT arthrogram status.
remediation_records.exact_policy_supported_requirement: Upper Extremity CT for joint/extremity pain is indicated ONLY if MRI is contraindicated or cannot be performed, OR requested as a CT arthrogram, preceded by negative/inconclusive plain radiographs and 4 weeks conservative therapy (Guideline 2062, physical pp. 965–966).

proposed_minimal_correction.summary: Add mandatory (mri_contraindicated == True OR requested_as_ct_arthrogram == True) prerequisite condition to existing Upper Extremity CT criteria.

criteria_spec.description: Upper extremity plain X-ray completed showing no definitive diagnostic etiology for joint/extremity pain
Persistent pain unresponsive to at least 4 weeks of active conservative therapy, OR acute complex fracture
Upper extremity MRI is contraindicated or cannot be performed, OR study is specifically requested as a CT arthrogram

citation_spec.source_quote:
X-rays must precede CT evaluation, unless otherwise indicated
If MRI is contraindicated or cannot be performed, or requested as a CT arthrogram

remediation_records.false_approval_risk: High. Approves diagnostic upper extremity CT for soft-tissue rotators, labrum, or cartilage tears where MRI is required.
remediation_records.false_denial_risk: Low. If patient has MRI contraindication or request is for CT arthrogram, CT is approved.

explicit_policy_requirements: Prior plain radiograph completed showing no clear etiology
Active conservative therapy failure >= 4 weeks OR acute bony fracture
MRI contraindicated OR cannot be performed OR requested as CT arthrogram
cumulative_conditions_and: Prior X-ray AND conservative care failure AND (MRI contraindication OR CT arthrogram)
advisory_or_preferred_language: MRI is the preferred modality for soft tissue, labral, and rotator cuff pathology
exceptions_and_special_populations: Preoperative surgical planning for complex comminuted fracture does not require conservative therapy

positive_cases.description: 4-week therapy failed, X-ray negative, pacemaker prevents MRI

remediation_records.current_behavior: Approves TMJ MRI (CPT 70336) based solely on symptom presentation (`suspected_tmj_internal_derangement == True`) without verifying prior conservative care.
remediation_records.exact_policy_supported_requirement: TMJ MRI for suspected internal derangement requires: persistent pain, clicking, or limitation of opening AND completion of at least 4 weeks of active conservative therapy (trial of pharmacotherapy AND behavioral modification) within the prior 6 months without meaningful improvement (Guideline 2055, physical p. 896).
remediation_records.governing_pdf: 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Advanced Imaging v2.pdf
remediation_records.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT (TMJ) MRI / Suspected Internal TMJ Derangement

proposed_minimal_correction.summary: Add mandatory 4-week conservative therapy failure requirement with pharmacotherapy and behavioral modification.

criteria_spec.description: Suspected internal derangement of the temporomandibular joint with mechanical locking, persistent pain, clicking, or limitation of mouth opening

Completion of at least 4 weeks of active conservative treatment including pharmacotherapy (NSAIDs/analgesics) AND behavioral modification (soft diet, jaw rest, moist heat, occlusal splint) within the prior 6 months

citation_spec.source_quote:
Suspected Internal TMJ Derangement
● Conservative therapy with a trial of pharmacotherapy* AND behavioral modification** for at least 4 weeks within the prior 6 months without meaningful improvement

remediation_records.false_approval_risk: High. Currently approves TMJ MRI immediately upon onset of jaw pain or clicking before trying oral analgesics or soft diet.
remediation_records.false_denial_risk: Low. If member has completed 4 weeks of medications and splinting/diet modification, rule approves cleanly.

explicit_policy_requirements: Conservative therapy >= 4 weeks within the prior 6 months
alternative_conditions_or: Acute closed lock of TMJ with inability to open mouth > 20 mm excuses conservative care
cumulative_conditions_and: Derangement symptoms AND conservative therapy duration >= 4 weeks
advisory_or_preferred_language: Initial plain radiographs or panoramic radiograph (Panorex) should be considered to rule out bony or odontogenic pathology
exceptions_and_special_populations: Acute locked jaw with sudden severe limitation of opening does not require 4 weeks of conservative care

positive_cases.description: Persistent jaw clicking and pain, 5 weeks of NSAIDs and occlusal splinting completed with no improvement

negative_cases.description: Jaw pain and clicking started 10 days ago, no medications or therapy tried

missing_evidence_cases.description: Jaw pain documented, conservative therapy duration not stated in records

conflicting_evidence_cases.description: Provider attests 4 weeks therapy, but pharmacy records show patient never filled NSAID or muscle relaxant prescription

boundary_value_cases.description: Exactly 4.0 weeks of conservative therapy documented

regression_assertions: Verify Maxillofacial CT (RULE-ADV-CG2047-001/002) routing is unaffected.
Verify Orbit/Face MRI (RULE-ADV-CG2048-001) routing is unaffected.

remediation_records.current_behavior: Approves Lower Extremity CT (CPT 73700-73702) for non-specific pain based on prior X-ray and MRI contraindication without checking conservative care.
remediation_records.exact_policy_supported_requirement: Lower extremity CT for non-specific pain requires: prior plain X-ray showing no clear etiology, MRI contraindicated or cannot be performed, AND failure of at least 4 weeks of active conservative therapy within the prior 6 months (or progression/worsening during therapy) (Guideline 2032, physical p. 504).
remediation_records.governing_pdf: 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Advanced Imaging v2.pdf
remediation_records.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR LOWER EXTREMITY CT / Non-specific Lower Extremity Pain (1,2)

proposed_minimal_correction.summary: Add mandatory 4-week conservative therapy failure condition within prior 6 months.

criteria_spec.description: Lower extremity pain without specific localized joint involvement
Prior plain radiographs (X-ray) completed of the symptomatic region
MRI is medically contraindicated or cannot be performed
Persistent pain unresponsive to at least 4 weeks of active conservative therapy within the prior 6 months, OR documented worsening during therapy

citation_spec.source_quote:
Lower extremity pain with no specific joint identified with MRI contraindicated or cannot be performed AND with prior X-ray showing no clear etiology of extremity pain with any ONE of the following:
● Persistent pain unresponsive to ACTIVE Conservative Therapy (ACT) for a minimum of 4 weeks in the last 6 months

remediation_records.false_approval_risk: High. Approves extremity CT prematurely when symptoms may resolve with standard physical therapy.
remediation_records.false_denial_risk: Low. Preserves access when 4 weeks of therapy or clinical worsening is documented.

explicit_policy_requirements: MRI contraindicated OR cannot be performed
Conservative therapy failure >= 4 weeks in prior 6 months OR worsening during therapy
alternative_conditions_or: Worsening of symptoms during conservative therapy
cumulative_conditions_and: Symptoms AND X-ray AND MRI contraindication AND conservative care
advisory_or_preferred_language: Active conservative therapy includes physical therapy, chiropractic treatments, or physician-directed home exercise program
exceptions_and_special_populations: Suspected acute fracture or pre-operative fracture planning (RULE-ADV-CG2032-002) bypasses conservative care

negative_cases.description: Leg pain, normal X-ray, pacemaker in place, but patient only did 1 week of rest

boundary_value_cases.description: Exactly 4 weeks of PT completed within prior 2 months

regression_assertions: Verify complex fracture rule (RULE-ADV-CG2032-002) still approves acute fractures without conservative care.
Verify Lower Extremity CTA (RULE-ADV-CG2033-001) is unaffected.

remediation_records.clinical_service_or_procedure: Lower Extremity MRI (Knee, Hip, Ankle, Foot)
remediation_records.current_behavior: Approves Lower Extremity MRI (CPT 73718-73723) based solely on `joint_specific_injury_or_pain == True`, omitting plain X-ray and conservative care requirements.
remediation_records.exact_policy_supported_requirement: Lower extremity MRI for joint-specific pain/injury requires: initial plain radiograph (X-ray) showing no clear etiology AND failure of at least 4 weeks of active conservative therapy within prior 6 months (unless acute mechanical locking or gross ligamentous instability) (Guideline 2035, physical p. 553).
remediation_records.governing_pdf: 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Advanced Imaging v2.pdf
remediation_records.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR LOWER EXTREMITY MRI / Joint Specific Pain or Suspected Joint Specific Injury

proposed_minimal_correction.summary: Add mandatory prior X-ray and 4-week conservative care failure conditions (with acute locking exception).

criteria_spec.description: Evaluation of joint-specific pain, mechanical locking, instability, or suspected internal derangement
Prior plain radiograph (X-ray) of the requested joint completed showing no clear explanation of symptoms
Failure of at least 4 weeks of active conservative therapy within prior 6 months, OR acute mechanical joint locking / acute gross ligamentous disruption

citation_spec.source_quote:
Joint specific advanced imaging is indicated with prior X-ray showing no clear etiology for the joint pain with any ONE of the following:
● Persistent joint pain unresponsive to ACTIVE Conservative Therapy (ACT) which includes physical therapy, chiropractic treatments, or a physician directed home exercise program (HEP) for a minimum of 4 weeks in the last 6 months

remediation_records.false_approval_risk: Severe. Currently approves high-volume MRI requests (CPT 73721 knee, 73718 foot/ankle, 73720 hip) on pain symptom check alone without any preliminary workup.
remediation_records.false_denial_risk: Low. If X-ray is done and 4 weeks therapy completed (or acute locked joint), rule approves.

cumulative_conditions_and: Joint pain AND prior X-ray AND (conservative care OR acute locking)
advisory_or_preferred_language: Weight-bearing X-rays are preferred for knee, ankle, and hip evaluations
exceptions_and_special_populations: Patients with positive knee orthopedic signs evaluate under RULE-ADV-CG2035-002
Suspected avascular necrosis evaluates under RULE-ADV-CG2035-003

remediation_records.clinical_service_or_procedure: Low Dose CT (LDCT) for Lung Cancer Screening
remediation_records.current_behavior: Approves LDCT (CPT 71271) based on age 50-80, >= 20 pack-years, and quit <= 15 yrs, without verifying that the patient is asymptomatic.
remediation_records.exact_policy_supported_requirement: LDCT lung cancer screening is medically necessary ONLY when used to screen for lung cancer for certain high-risk, ASYMPTOMATIC individuals (i.e. no acute lung-related signs or symptoms such as hemoptysis, unexplained cough, shortness of breath, unexplained weight loss) (Guideline 2030, physical p. 490).
remediation_records.governing_pdf: 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Advanced Imaging v2.pdf
remediation_records.source_section: INDICATIONS / For Annual Screening / Group 1 - High Risk for Lung Cancer (3,4)

proposed_minimal_correction.summary: Add mandatory patient_is_asymptomatic == True screening restriction condition.

criteria_spec.description: Patient is asymptomatic with no acute lung-related signs or symptoms (e.g. hemoptysis, unexplained persistent cough, unexplained weight loss)
Patient age is between 50 and 80 years old
Documented smoking history of at least 20 pack-years
Patient is currently smoking or has quit smoking within the past 15 years

citation_spec.source_quote: medically necessary ONLY when used to screen for lung cancer for certain high-risk, asymptomatic individuals (i.e., no acute lung-related signs or symptoms)

remediation_records.false_approval_risk: Severe patient safety risk. Approves screening LDCT for a symptomatic patient with active hemoptysis or lung tumor, missing diagnostic full-dose contrast evaluation.
remediation_records.false_denial_risk: Low. Asymptomatic individuals meeting USPSTF criteria are approved.

explicit_policy_requirements: Patient must be asymptomatic for pulmonary disease
Current smoker OR quit within past 15 years
cumulative_conditions_and: Asymptomatic AND age 50-80 AND >= 20 pack-years AND (current smoker OR quit <= 15 yrs)
advisory_or_preferred_language: Screening should be discontinued once a person develops a health problem that limits life expectancy
exceptions_and_special_populations: Symptomatic patients should be redirected to Diagnostic Chest CT (CPT 71250-71270, RULE-ADV-CG2018-*)

positive_cases.description: Asymptomatic 62yo, 30 pack-year smoker who quit 5 years ago

negative_cases.description: 65yo 25-pack-year smoker presents with gross hemoptysis and 15lb weight loss
Asymptomatic 60yo, 25 pack-years, but quit 16 years ago

conflicting_evidence_cases.description: Intake form marked 'asymptomatic' but clinical notes mention 'unexplained hemoptysis for 2 weeks'

regression_assertions: Verify Diagnostic Chest CT (CPT 71250-71270) routes to RULE-ADV-CG2018-* and evaluates hemoptysis correctly.
Verify Chest CTA (RULE-ADV-CG2020-*) is unaffected.

remediation_records.clinical_service_or_procedure: Quantitative Computed Tomography (QCT) Bone Density Study
remediation_records.current_behavior: Approves QCT Bone Density (CPT 77078) based solely on `suspected_low_bone_mineral_density == True`, omitting mandatory DXA unavailability and body habitus prerequisites.
remediation_records.exact_policy_supported_requirement: QCT bone density study is indicated for suspected osteopenia/osteoporosis ONLY after meeting any ONE of: (1) DXA scanning is expected to be insufficient OR is not available, (2) advanced degenerative changes of spine, or (3) severe obesity with BMI > 35 kg/m2 (Guideline 2024, physical pp. 451–452).
remediation_records.governing_pdf: 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Advanced Imaging v2.pdf
remediation_records.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR CT BONE DENSITY STUDY / Screening for Asymptomatic Low Bone Mineral Density

proposed_minimal_correction.summary: Add mandatory general criteria requiring DXA insufficiency/unavailability, advanced spine degeneration, or BMI > 35.

criteria_spec.description: Screening or diagnostic assessment of low bone mineral density (osteopenia or osteoporosis)
Meets at least one general prerequisite: DXA scanning is insufficient/unavailable, advanced spinal degenerative changes, or severe obesity (BMI > 35 kg/m2)

citation_spec.source_quote:
A CT bone density study (Quantitative CT (QCT)) is indicated for screening for asymptomatic low BMD after meeting any ONE of the following general criteria:
● Dual x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scanning is expected to be insufficient OR is not available
● Patients with advanced degenerative changes of the spine
● Severe obesity (BMI > 35 kg/m2)

remediation_records.false_approval_risk: High. Approves QCT (which has significantly higher radiation dose than DXA) without requiring standard first-line DXA testing.
remediation_records.false_denial_risk: Low. Patients with BMI > 35, spinal degenerative disease, or lack of local DXA scanner approve cleanly.

explicit_policy_requirements: At least ONE general prerequisite: DXA insufficient/unavailable, severe obesity (BMI > 35), or advanced spinal degenerative changes
cumulative_conditions_and: Low bone mineral density suspected AND (DXA insufficient OR spine degeneration OR BMI > 35)
advisory_or_preferred_language: DXA is the gold standard initial study and requires less radiation than QCT
exceptions_and_special_populations: Washington State specific legislative language mandates must be respected if jurisdiction is WA

positive_cases.description: Osteoporosis screening in 67yo female with BMI 38 (exceeds DXA table limit)
Patient with severe lumbar scoliosis and degenerative osteophytes falsely elevating DXA

missing_evidence_cases.description: Low bone density suspected, but DXA status and BMI omitted

boundary_value_cases.description: BMI exactly 35.1 kg/m2 satisfies severe obesity criterion

regression_assertions: Verify standard CT procedures (RULE-ADV-CG2000-*) are unaffected.
